## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Release gate: unit-stage hang bound aborts green full-suite runs on a contended host

> **Status: intake DRAFT — two questions are open (see [Open Questions](#open-questions-blocking-intake-completion)).**
> Stage remains `idea` until the producer answers Q1 (bound strategy) and Q2 (cross-repo scope for
> the cache-resume path); the next `/skill:intake` run finalises this brief from those answers.

## Problem statement

The dev→main release gate aborted the v0.1.24 release with a `[hang-timeout]` (exit 124) from the
**unit** stage even though no test was red: the stage was still working through 241 files when the
300 s wall-clock bound fired, on a host running three concurrent test runs plus a Monte-Carlo sweep
(16 cores, load average reported as 35–42). The gate cannot currently distinguish "the suite is red"
from "the host is busy", so contention fails a green release and costs a 20+ minute full re-run.

## Users

- **Producer running a release** (`/skill:ship release`) — needs the gate's verdict to be trustworthy
  on a busy machine: contention must read as contention, and a retry must not re-execute a stage that
  is already known-green.
- **Agent sessions sharing the host** — several worktrees run `run_tests.py --scope changed`
  concurrently by design; they must not be able to fail each other's release gate.

User stories:

- As a producer running a release on a contended host, I want the hang diagnostic to show the stage,
  the bound, the elapsed time and the host load, so I can tell contention from a genuine hang without
  opening the cache entry.
- As a producer, I want the unit-stage bound to have enough headroom for the worst green run I have
  actually observed on this host, so a busy machine cannot abort a green release.
- As a producer, I want a unit-stage abort to be resumable from an existing green full-suite cache
  entry (same tree, within TTL) instead of re-running the whole suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` /
  `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time,
  the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention is
  distinguishable from a genuine hang without reading `.worklog/cache/<key>/`.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the existing browser-stage paragraph
  (starved `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`)
  is not printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound (`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`) no longer aborts a run at the worst
  contention observed on this host: the chosen bound/mechanism is justified against the measured
  baseline (recent green unit stages: 88 s, 96 s, 106 s, 111 s, 128 s, 141 s, 147 s, 149 s, 206 s,
  217 s — worst observed green 217 s; nominal < 2 min), and that justification is recorded in the
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header comment and in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.
- The inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer release-gate budget: the sum of stage bounds
  cannot silently exceed the outer `timeoutPerCommand` (1500 s in `.pi/test-config.json`) without the
  outer timeout being adjusted in the same change, and the invariant (worst observed full suite plus
  the new unit bound still fits) is stated in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.
- A unit-stage hang no longer forces a full re-run of the release when the tree is unchanged: the
  resume path from a green cached full-suite entry is available (a hang's 124 entry does not destroy a
  green entry for the same tree state) and is documented, with the cache TTL gate intact; the
  implementation repository for this criterion is settled by Q2.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124`, `HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`, never retried, and the
  `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` covers the new diagnostic content (stage, bound,
  elapsed, delta, load average) and the bound/load behaviour, with the load average injected through a
  test seam so the assertions are deterministic and never read the real host.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and
  any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried"
  (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) and the project-coverage fail-closed behaviour (CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H) are
  invariants: a genuine hang must still surface, and a bound that is too generous to fire is a
  regression in the opposite direction.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable (`--timeout-ms`) — a
  load-aware bound is an addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and CI hosts with a
  different core count must still get a sane bound.
- **Determinism in tests.** No test may read the real load average; sample it behind an injectable seam.
- **Repository boundaries.** `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`,
  `tests/**,` `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `.pi/test-config.json` are in this repo. The release gate
  script and the read-only test cache are **not**: they live in the agent framework repo
  (SorraAgents) and must not be edited without explicit instruction — see Q2.
- **Scope discipline.** A load-aware outer gate timeout, stage-level parallel resume, or per-file
  retry budgets are out of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.

## Existing state

- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` runs four stages; the unit stage passes `--timeout-ms 300000` (line 92)
  and the browser stage `--timeout-ms 1200000` (line 96). Its header comment (lines ~50–59) documents
  the bounds and why the browser bound was raised.
- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` bounds every attempt (`runVitestProcess`), computes
  `elapsedSecs`, and on overrun prints `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs)`, which reports
  "did not complete within {elapsed}s" — conflating elapsed with the bound — and prints a
  browser-specific cause list unconditionally. Nothing samples `os.loadavg()`, and the stage
  (`--project …`) is only visible in the trailing `[vitest-runner] attempts=… args="--project unit"`
  summary line.
- The release gate is `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` →
  `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` (no `--timeout`, so
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` from `.pi/test-config.json` applies to the whole `npm --silent test`
  command). TCE's documented full-suite time is 18–21 min, i.e. ~4–7 min of headroom.
- The per-repo cache stores the full run output (`metadata.json`, `stdout.txt`, `stderr.txt`) in
  `.worklog/cache/<sha>/`, keyed on command + git state, TTL 2 h; a hang **does** overwrite the
  cache entry for that state with `exit_code: 124`, which is why a retry re-runs everything.
- Evidence from the aborted run: cache entry `3b6572d09f1a6363f3a1be3d020af939`
  (`exit_code: 124`, note `suite exited 124 with no parsable failures`, facts
  `elapsed=311.09s, configured_timeout=1500s`); its `stdout.txt` ends with the 300 s
  `[hang-timeout]`, the browser-only advice, and
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
  The slowest unit file in that run was `tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` at 55.8 s (two full
  `vite build`s).

### Evidence corrections (capture fidelity)

- The item description says "A retry at load ~8 was accepted, so the bound — not the code — was the
  failure mode", citing `/tmp/ship-release-20261113-002647.log`. That log records the *producer-review
  gate* blocking the release (CG-0MW3KV4D7004KCF0, CG-0MWC07OBB004YD5E); it contains **no** test-stage
  output, so it is not evidence of a green retry. The correct conclusions still stand — the aborted
  entry had no failing test and the same suite is green at other times — but the specific retry claim
  is unsupported and should not be quoted as evidence.
- The load average of 35–42 is the discovery session's host observation and is not recorded in either
  log; it is treated here as an assertion of the discovering agent, not as measured evidence. Sampling
  the load average at abort (AC 1) is what makes it measurable next time.

## Desired change

1. **Diagnose.** Extend the hang diagnostic (and keep it cheap) to carry stage, bound, elapsed, delta,
   load average and core count, with stage-appropriate guidance. Take the load sample at abort and,
   ideally, one at start so the delta is meaningful; keep it behind an injectable sampler for tests.
2. **Bound.** Adopt the Q1 decision for the unit stage (recommended: a raised static floor plus
   load-aware scaling up to a ceiling) and reconcile it with the 1500 s outer budget — either scaling
   the outer timeout in the same change or documenting why it still fits.
3. **Resume.** Adopt the Q2 decision for the green-entry resume path, so a unit-stage abort does not
   force a 20+ minute re-run of an unchanged tree.
4. **Test and document.** Cover the diagnostic and bound logic in
   `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`; update `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
   (§ Test Configuration, § Hang timeout) and the `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — hang diagnostic content (stage/bound/elapsed/delta/load,
  stage-specific guidance), load-average sampling seam, bound derivation.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — unit-stage `--timeout-ms`, header comment rationale.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — diagnostic + bound coverage with injected load.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — hang-timeout section (~line 1313) and test-config section (~line 816).
- `.pi/test-config.json` — `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` if the outer budget is adjusted.
- *(Q2-dependent, agent framework repo)* `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`,
  `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — green-entry
  preservation / resume path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — a bound that never fires.** A raised or load-scaled bound can mask a genuine hang; the
  mitigation is to keep the ceiling finite, keep exit 124 and the never-retry rule, and print the
  bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Risk — outer timeout becomes the new abort point.** Raising the unit bound without touching the
  1500 s outer budget moves the failure from a clear `[hang-timeout]` to an opaque outer kill
  (`suite exited 124`, no stage detail). Mitigated by the AC that keeps inner and outer budgets
  reconciled.
- **Risk — host-specific tuning leaks into CI.** A load-aware bound calibrated on this 16-core
  workstation may under-bound a smaller CI runner; the floor must be safe on any host.
- **Risk — flaky diagnostics tests.** Reading `/proc/loadavg` in a test makes assertions
  environment-dependent; the load sample must be injectable.
- **Assumption** — the load average of 35–42 comes from the discovery session's observation, not from
  a log; AC 1 makes it measurable rather than relying on recollection.
- **Assumption** — the v0.1.24 release was ultimately unblocked by the producer-review gate, so no
  *test* evidence from a later green retry is available (see Evidence corrections).
- **Scope-creep risk** — a fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout, stage-level parallel resume, and
  per-file retry budgets are plausible follow-ups; record them as linked work items rather than
  growing this change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** — "Browser test stage hangs on gym overlay tests during full-suite npm test
  under CPU contention" (completed): the precedent for this item — it introduced the bounded
  wall-clock abort, `HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE = 124`, the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound
  15 → 20 min after normal variance straddled the old limit. This item is the same failure mode one
  stage earlier, at a bound that has only ~1.4× headroom over the worst observed green unit run.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** — project-coverage gate (`expected=241 ran=indeterminate` in the aborted
  entry comes from it); its fail-closed behaviour must be preserved.
- **CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F**, **CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU**, **CG-0MVNDK56G007C1U7** — retry/transient
  acceptance semantics that sit beside the hang path in the same runner.
- **CG-0MVWFLG8Z005FSH8** — precedent for carrying release-shaped rationale in the
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header comment.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout (line 1313), § Test Configuration (line 816);
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`.
- Framework (SorraAgents): `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` (the release gate),
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (cache client), `skill/test_cache.py` (TTL, lookup/store).

## Open Questions (blocking intake completion)

**Q1 — Which bound strategy should the unit stage adopt (AC 2)?**

- **A. Raise the static bound** (e.g. 300 s → 600 s), justified against the worst observed green run
  (217 s). Simple, one number, easy to reason about; but headroom is still a guess and a busier day
  re-opens the item.
- **B. Load-aware bound only** — scale the bound by the sampled 1-min load average relative to the
  core count, with a floor. Adapts to contention; but it hides a slow-but-genuine hang behind a
  rising bound and makes the abort point host-dependent.
- **C. Hybrid (static floor + load-aware scaling up to a ceiling), with the outer 1500 s gate budget
  reconciled in the same change.** Keeps a predictable floor, absorbs contention, and closes the
  "inner bounds exceed the outer timeout" hole.

**Recommended:** C — the evidence (worst green run 217 s against a 300 s bound, ~4–7 min of outer
headroom) shows a single static number either stays fragile or eats the whole outer budget, while a
pure load-aware bound weakens hang detection.

**Q2 — Where should the green-cache-entry resume path (AC 4) be implemented?**

- **A. Document only, in this repo** — describe the resume procedure and leave the cache/gate code
  untouched (no code change for AC 4).
- **B. Split: keep this CG item for the TCE-side bound + diagnostic, and file the cache/gate change as
  a linked SorraAgents work item (SA-…) that this item depends on.**
- **C. Do the framework change inside this item**, editing `skill/test/…` and
  `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly (precedent: CG-0MUFIBB2X008A136 was
  implemented in SorraAgents).

**Recommended:** B — the release gate and cache live in the agent framework repo, and editing
`skill/` is out of bounds without explicit instruction; a linked SA item keeps the change auditable
there while this item stays self-contained.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (bound strategy: static raise / load-aware only / hybrid) — OPEN QUESTION, pending producer
  answer.** Asked 2026-11-13 in intake for CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09. Agent recommendation: C (hybrid,
  with the outer 1500 s budget reconciled). Research: `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` (bounds at lines 56,
  92, 96); `.pi/test-config.json` (`timeoutPerCommand: 1500`) and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` line 816
  ("full suite takes 18–21 minutes"); measured green unit-stage durations from
  `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` (88–217 s, worst 217 s on 2026-11-11 17:37); no load-average
  awareness exists anywhere in `scripts/` today.
- **Q2 (cross-repo scope for the green-entry resume path) — OPEN QUESTION, pending producer answer.**
  Asked 2026-11-13 in intake for CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09. Agent recommendation: B (split into a linked
  SorraAgents item). Research: `merge-dev-to-main.sh` resolves the runner from
  `$REPO_ROOT/skill/test/…` or `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/…`; this repo has no `skill/` tree and
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`; the cache TTL
  (2 h) and store/lookup live in `skill/test_cache.py` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- **Duplicate check** — searched `wl search "hang timeout vitest retry"`: the closest item,
  CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N (browser-stage hang bound), is completed and does not cover the unit-stage
  bound, the diagnostic content, or the resume path; no duplicate found.


---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** – Browser test stage hangs on gym overlay tests during full-suite npm test under CPU contention (completed)
- **CG-0MT4ASE64003CBEK** – Verify: full test suite and build pass after multiplier retune (completed)
- **CG-0MSKVOSW3004HZVB** – Verify full suite green with documented deps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`

# Test skill: run_tests.py reports a retry-accepted stage as FAIL (exit 0, `outcome=retry-clean`)

## Problem statement

`scripts/run_tests.py` (the shared test skill) harvests failure names from a
stage's **combined output** (`parse_failures`) even when the stage's own retry
runner (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) already discarded the failing attempt and
returned **exit 0**. A `retry-clean` stage is therefore reported as a suite
failure and the dev→main release gate blocks a genuinely green tree — observed
during the v0.1.24 release of Tableau-Card-Engine (merged tree, load ~7).

## Users

- **Release engineer** (primary): runs the ship skill's release gate
  (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` → `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`).
  User story: "As a release engineer, I want a stage the project's own retry
  runner already accepted (`outcome=retry-clean` / `accepted-transient`) to be
  reported green, so a contention flake the runner already recovered from does
  not block a release whose code is sound."
- **Audit consumers**: `audit_runner.py` shares `parse_failures` for F-cache
  misses; its verdicts should classify the same way (green after accepted
  retry, never `unparsed_failure`).
- **Operators triaging a red run**: want to see *which file flaked* on the
  discarded attempt as diagnostics, not as a suite failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a command's output carries the retry runner's final green verdict
      (`[vitest-runner] ... status=0 outcome=retry-clean` or
      `status=0 outcome=accepted-transient`), `parse_failures` discards the
      failure names harvested from the superseded attempt and the suite
      reports success (`success=True`, `failures=[]`).
- [ ] The masking guards are unchanged: a stage whose retry ends
      `outcome=retry-failed` / `outcome=failed` (or any non-zero `status` on
      the runner line), or a stage with **no** retry banner, still reports
      every genuine failure (per-stage segmentation: only failures from
      green-verdict stages are discarded, so a retry-clean browser stage never
      masks a genuine unit/tutorial failure in the same `npm test` output).
- [ ] The discarded-attempt failures remain visible as diagnostics (not as
      suite failures) — e.g. a notice/`notice_code` naming the flaked file
      and/or a structured JSON field on the suite result — so an operator can
      still see which file flaked.
- [ ] Unit tests (SorraAgents `skill/test/tests/`) cover: (a) retry-clean
      output with a failed first attempt → green; (b) retry-failed output →
      red with the failures listed; (c) genuine-failure-only output (no
      banner / no retry) → red, unchanged; (d) mixed output where only the
      green-verdict stage's failures are discarded.
- [ ] The release gate (`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` →
      `run_tests.py --scope full`) no longer needs a re-run after an accepted
      retry, verified with the captured cache entry
      (`.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193`) replaying green.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — module and
      function docstrings in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (the
      `parse_failures`/`parse_vitest_failures` contract) and any
      `docs/dev/*` pages that enumerate failure classification/outcomes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (SorraAgents:
      `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full` from the
      SorraAgents repo — the shared-skill suite; neither repo's suite is
      degraded by the parser change). CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.

## Impact

A release whose browser stage flaked once and was recovered by the retry runner
now passes the gate on the first run instead of forcing the operator to
re-run the full suite to prove a green tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repo boundary (assumption):** the change is made in the SorraAgents
  checkout where the code is versioned; this CG item records it. If the
  producer prefers a WL mirror item, planning may create it — the code change
  is identical either way (see Constraints *tracking decision*).
- **Additive result fields only:** surfacing discarded failures must be
  additive (`discarded_failures`/notice), never remove or rename existing
  suite/aggregate result keys consumers (`run_cached` metadata, audit, ship
  gate) rely on.
- **Shared-parser regression risk:** `parse_failures` is consumed by the audit
  too; AC7 (full suite) and the unchanged-path unit tests guard this. A
  mis-parsed verdict only ever *keeps* failures (red), never drops a genuine
  one — fail-safe direction.
- **Scope creep:** per-stage JSON diagnostics, cache-format changes, or
  altering the retry runner are out of scope; any follow-ups become linked
  work items, not part of this fix.

## Constraints

- **Code location is the shared agent-framework repo, not this repo.** The
  canonical `run_tests.py` lives at
  `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (symlinked into
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); it is NOT tracked in
  Tableau-Card-Engine. Tests live in `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/`
  (`test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py` is the primary target for parser unit
  tests). Implementation therefore happens in the SorraAgents checkout, whose
  own repo gates (build → test → commit; `dev`-only pushes) apply. **Tracking
  decision (assumption, flag for producer):** this CG item stays the tracker
  here; the cross-repo change is recorded on it per the repo-boundary rules
  (never edit `.pi/`/`skill/` trees from TCE unless explicitly instructed —
  this item IS the explicit instruction for `run_tests.py`). If the producer
  prefers a SorraAgents `WL` mirror item, that may be created at planning; the
  code change itself is identical.
- **Do not change the retry runner's semantics.** The fix is in the
  *consumer* (`parse_failures`); `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` already guarantees
  `retry-clean` means the second attempt passed and `accepted-transient` means
  every error block was attributable to an acceptable transient signature.
- **Token name:** the ACs' "transient-accepted" corrects to the runner's
  actual token `outcome=accepted-transient` (emitted by
  `vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, `runSummary(..., 'accepted-transient', ...)`).
  Both green tokens (`retry-clean`, `accepted-transient`) must be honoured;
  `status=0` must accompany them.
- **Multiple runner lines:** `npm --silent test` runs several stages; each
  retry-runner stage emits its own `[vitest-runner]` line. Green verdicts must
  be attributed per stage/segment so a genuine failure elsewhere in the same
  command is never masked.
- **Shared consumers:** `parse_failures` is imported by both
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`run_suite`) and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; both must classify consistently.
- **Fixture evidence:** the exact output shape is captured at
  `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193/`
  (unit `outcome=clean`, browser FAIL block, `[retry]` banner, browser
  `outcome=retry-clean`, exit 0) and `/tmp/ship-release-20261113-042438.log`.

## Existing state

- `run_tests.py` (shared test skill) routes Vitest output into
  `parse_vitest_failures` (MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS); Vitest browser output like
  `FAIL |browser (chromium)|
  tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts` parses into a
  structured record from the `Failed Tests` block.
- The retry runner (`Tableau-Card-Engine/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`)
  emits a final machine-readable
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=... expected=N ran=M` line to
  stderr after every attempt sequence (outcomes: `clean`, `failed`,
  `retry-clean`, `retry-failed`, `accepted-transient`, `coverage-failed`,
  `hang`).
- `run_suite` builds `success = overall_returncode == 0 and not all_failures`;
  on the v0.1.24 run `npm --silent test` exited 0 but `all_failures` contained
  the browser file parsed from the superseded first attempt → stage reported
  `FAIL ... exit_code=0` and the release needed a re-run.
- `run_tests.py` currently treats the `[vitest-runner]` line only as a block
  terminator in the Vitest parser (`_VITEST_BLOCK_END_RE`); it never inspects
  the verdict.

## Desired change

- In the shared failure-parsing entry point (`parse_failures`), segment the
  command output by the runner's `[vitest-runner]` verdict lines. For a
  segment whose verdict is `status=0` + (`retry-clean` | `accepted-transient`),
  harvest the failures from that stage so they can be reported as discarded
  diagnostics, but return no suite-failure records from it. Segments with a
  non-green verdict (any non-zero `status`, or no banner at all) keep the
  current behaviour — every genuine failure is reported.
- Preserve the discarded names as diagnostics: a notice/`notice_code` (and/or
  a structured field on the suite result, e.g. `discarded_failures`) naming
  the flaked file(s), so an operator can see what the retry recovered.
- Keep the route shared: because the change lives in `parse_failures`, the
  audit's failure harvesting classifies identically.
- Land with unit tests in `skill/test/tests/` covering green/red/unchanged
  paths including a mixed-output case; replay the captured cache entry as the
  canonical retry-clean fixture.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `parse_failures`,
  `parse_vitest_failures`, `run_suite` (`_result`/`success`), `run_all`
  (aggregate failures/notices) — add the retry-verdict discard + diagnostics.
- `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py` — parser unit
  tests (existing fixture-driven coverage for FAIL blocks, trees, frames).
- `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` /
  `test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` — suite-level/notice coverage for the
  diagnostics field if the implementation surfaces one.
- `SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — shared consumer; verify
  (no change expected) that its failure harvesting classifies retry-clean as
  green.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193/`
  (stdout.txt + metadata.json exit_code 0) — canonical retry-clean fixture.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — reference for the
  runner verdict contract (read-only; do not change).
- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — the release
  gate that consumes the verdict (AC5 verification point; no change expected).

## Related work

- `SorraAgents/Skill` items (WL):
  - SA-0MW3GCRWE0061VDW — "Test skill: aggregate state_changed_during_run
    notice and drop failures" — the direct precedent: a flagged command's
    parsed failures are dropped from suite/aggregate and surfaced as a
    stable notice; this item follows the same pattern for the retry verdict
    (see the `state_changed_flag` short-circuit in `run_suite`).
  - SA-0MSAC1BIP004IQ3T / SA-0MSAC1BG6000Z1CM — run_tests.py runner + tests.
  - MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS — Vitest failure parsing (the FAIL-block parser this
    fix extends).
  - Duplicate check performed (wl search terms: "retry-clean",
    "parse_failures retry", "release gate retry stage", plus completed-item
    search) — no overlapping completed or open item found; this CG item is the
    only tracker for the parser-side discard.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine` items (CG):
  - CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3 / CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE / CG-0MVNDK56G007C1U7 /
    CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N / CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F / CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU /
    CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H — the contention-signature retry work in
    `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` whose outcome tokens this fix consumes.
  - CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09 — "Release gate: unit-stage 300s hang bound aborts
    full-suite runs on a contended host" (open; related release-gate
    robustness concern, not a duplicate — different stage/verdict).

## Related work (automated report)

- **CG-0MU4U38HU000AXU2** — [test-failure] `<suite exited 1>: npm --silent
  test — failing test` (completed) — retry-attributable failure surfaced by
  the same `npm test` command shape.
- **CG-0MQ1HJIL8000EPKV** — [Test] HUD Layer Contract Tests (completed).
- **CG-0MQN0TW5M000ADLL** — F3: DurationEventCard type & tests (completed).
- Repository matches: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  (keyword overlap only; no code overlap).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The code change lives in the SorraAgents repo (shared skill) while this
  item is CG-tracked in Tableau-Card-Engine — should the work be implemented
  from this CG item (cross-repo, recorded here) or mirrored as a SorraAgents
  WL item?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded for the producer; the brief assumes
  the former with the code change being identical either way). Answering party:
  producer at review/plan. Research: `run_tests.py` resolves to
  `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (verified via
  `readlink -f`/inode); TCE has no copy; the release gate lives in
  `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`; SA-0MW3GCRWE0061VDW
  is the same script fixed from a WL item.
- Q: "The AC wording 'transient-accepted' — the runner actually emits
  `accepted-transient`." — Answer (agent, from source):
  `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` emits `outcome=accepted-transient`
  (`runSummary(..., 'accepted-transient', ...)`); the AC text above uses
  `accepted-transient`. Source: source code is more authoritative than the
  work item; no user confirmation needed.
- No further interview questions: the seed context (evidence section, cache
  entry, release log) sufficed to draft the brief; no answers were required to
